messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The test `testLang412Left` calls `StrBuilder.appendFixedWidthPadLeft(null, 10, '*')`. The main issue is that this call leads to a NullPointerException (NPE) when `getNullText()` has not been set (i.e., it returns null).

Looking at the implementation of the method `appendFixedWidthPadLeft(Object obj, int width, char padChar)`:
- It first checks if width is greater than 0.
- It calls `ensureCapacity(size + width)` to make sure the backing buffer is large enough.
- It then converts the passed object to a String by doing `String str = (obj == null ? getNullText() : obj.toString());`.
- If `obj` is null, it uses the result of `getNullText()`.
- However, if `getNullText()` returns null (which is the default if not explicitly set), the variable `str` becomes null.
- Then the code tries to call `str.length()` which throws NullPointerException because `str` is null.

The constructor `StrBuilder()` initializes the internal char buffer but does not set any null text by default (it appears `nullText` field is null initially, confirmed by `getNullText()` simply returning `nullText` field).

Hence, the root cause: `appendFixedWidthPadLeft` does not handle well the case when a null object is passed and no null text has been configured. It should either:
- Provide a default for null text internally (e.g., use the string `"null"` instead of null), or
- Handle the case where `getNullText()` returns null before calling `str.length()`.

This behavior matches exactly the issue described in the bug report: "Appending a null value with fixed width causes a null pointer exception if getNullText() has not been set."

Recent bug reports about other issues are not relevant here.

Overall, the bug occurs because the method assumes that `getNullText()` never returns null, which is not the case by default, leading to an NPE when appending null objects with fixed width padding.

The fix should involve checking if `str` is null after getting `getNullText()` and providing a fallback string before using it.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
